- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.17) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–7 days.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.3), model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–4% for next 3–5 days.  
- Model often overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., >70) — cap forecast at +5% above peak for 3–5 days.  
- If 3+ consecutive forecast days are above 70, apply mean reversion: subtract 0.5–1.5% per day until price stabilizes.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates >5% from 14-day moving average, adjust forecast toward that average.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– swings (e.g., +0.17, -0.28, +0.17), model tends to lag — forecast 1–2 days ahead of true trend.  
- When sentiment is flat (0.00) for 3+ days, model often fails to capture mean reversion — apply 0.5–1.0% downward correction.
